newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end lower despite Dow's advance.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end lower despite Dow's advance.

text.p: Manila shares finished weaker on Wednesday after drifting in a narrow band for most of the session unconvinced by the Dow's gains, traders said.
"Wall Street's rise was not enough and sentiments remained negative," said Poch Zamora, dealer at Peregrine Securities.
The market's main barometer slipped by 9.58 points, or 0.30 percent, closing at 3,162.21 points.

All sub-indices fell with only the oil sector bucking the trend. The property sector posted the biggest loss on rumours Empire East Land Inc was facing financial difficulties, but this was immediately denied by the company.
"Market is still negative and people are still waiting for first quarter corporate earnings results," said Jose Ricardo Garcia, executive vice-president at Diversified Securities.
Rudsend Alpay, Lippo Securities assistant vice-president, said he expects the eagerly-awaited listing of Equitable Banking Corp on Thursday to renew investor interest in the equities market.
Garcia said that with additional liquidity pumped into the system, funds will likely be plowed back to second and thirdliners.
